metrics.name: max_rel_error
metrics.method: max |u_num - u_exact| / amplitude at t = steps*dt against the closed-form solution

metrics.name: conservation_drift
metrics.method: |mean(u_T) - mean(u_0)|; the periodic Laplacian conserves the mean exactly in exact arithmetic

metrics.name: throughput_mlups
metrics.method: n*n*steps / wall time of the final sweep, time.perf_counter inside the workload

metrics.name: step_seconds
metrics.method: wall time of the final sweep

metrics.name: field_sum
metrics.method: sum of the final field, used for cross-implementation agreement

metrics.name: diffusion_number
metrics.method: r = alpha*dt/h^2, held at 0.1 for this workload

metrics.name: total_time
metrics.method: steps*dt, the physical time reached by the run

criteria.rationale: FTCS truncation is O(dt)+O(h^2). With h=1/96, dt=0.1*h^2/alpha the a-priori bound is about 1e-3 relative amplitude; 3e-3 gives a 3x margin. Fixed before the first run.
Same truncation argument in the L2 norm; the L2 error cannot exceed the max-norm error by more than the domain area factor.
A periodic five-point Laplacian annihilates constants, so the discrete mean is conserved up to float64 round-off; 1e-9 is ~1e7 ulp of the field mean.

reference.source: u(x,y,t)=A*exp(-2*alpha*k^2*t)*sin(kx)*sin(ky), k=2*pi/L, exact solution of u_t=alpha*(u_xx+u_yy) on the periodic square

acceptance.policy: criteria are declared in this file and hashed into provenance.criteria_sha256; a run cannot pass by relaxing them

comparison.hypothesis: The row-slice zip kernel is >=10% faster in throughput than the index-arithmetic kernel at identical numerical results
